companies.name: Walmart
companies.boundary: Direct refrigerant emissions; energy and lifecycle effects excluded
companies.summary: A major source of warming sits inside the cooling systems that keep groceries fresh. Existing CO₂ systems can sharply reduce direct refrigerant impact in suitable stores.
companies.opportunity: Finance refrigeration replacement and installation capacity.
constraints: Eligible share is assumed, not measured. It refers to emissions, not store count.
Study transfer needs validation for Walmart’s gas mix, store climate, leakage and equipment age.
Additional electricity, fuel and embodied impacts must be deducted for net savings.
Existing and already committed conversions do not establish additional fund impact.
steps: Walmart reports 4.08 million tonnes CO₂e from onsite refrigerants.
A paired supermarket study reported 191 versus 0.1 tonnes of direct refrigerant impact at equal leaked mass. Whole-store emissions differed by about 15%, not 99.95%.
Apply the direct reduction factor only to an explicitly assumed share of eligible converted emissions.
Value that physical difference at $255.12 per tonne, leaving unmeasured lifecycle effects visible.

companies.name: ExxonMobil
companies.boundary: Tank methane after recovered-gas combustion; other lifecycle effects excluded
companies.summary: Methane escaping from storage can be captured at suitable sources. The climate benefit must count the CO₂ released when recovered methane is burned.
companies.formula: 6,816 t CH₄ × assumed eligible untreated share × 95% × (29.8 − 2.75)
companies.opportunity: Finance eligible vapor recovery equipment with measured leak reduction.
constraints: The source pool is inferred from rounded shares, not a list of untreated eligible tanks.
The 25%, 50% and 100% cases are assumptions, not a confidence interval.
Compression power, downstream leakage, other hydrocarbons and equipment impacts remain unquantified.
No displacement of other gas production is assumed. Fund additionality and repayment need project evidence.
steps: Reported methane of 142,000 tonnes × 96% upstream × 5% tanks implies about 6,816 tonnes CH₄.
EPA gives 95% control for suitable vapor recovery sources.
Convert fossil methane at GWP100 29.8 and subtract 2.75 tonnes CO₂ per tonne of recovered methane burned.
Apply an explicit eligible untreated share; subtract other lifecycle effects when data becomes available.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.boundary: Study-matched annualized virtual-core service; no company-scale estimate
companies.summary: Cooling design can reduce the lifecycle footprint of equivalent compute service. Research supports a process improvement; the eligible Microsoft fleet is still unknown.
companies.opportunity: Identify suitable unconverted compute cohorts, then assess retrofit finance.
constraints: 15% is a study-matched process comparison, not Microsoft’s company gap.
Study assumptions include 20% overclocking, 28% more virtual cores, a 2021 US grid and specified asset lives.
The 31% blue-water reduction is a separate lifecycle metric and cannot be applied to company onsite water.
Eligible unconverted fleet and its matching lifecycle baseline are missing.
sources: Technology · Nature lifecycle cooling study, Table 4
steps: Use the source’s annualized virtual-core functional unit to preserve equivalent service.
The study models 15% lower lifecycle climate impact for cold plates under its assumptions.
Normalize to 1,000 baseline lifecycle tonnes: 150 tonnes reduction.
Do not scale to the company until the matching eligible cohort is known.

companies.name: Nucor
companies.boundary: Comparable unoptimized furnace electricity; no climate-damage estimate
companies.summary: Nucor already uses electric-arc furnaces. A demonstrated controls upgrade is a more relevant opportunity than pretending it could switch away from blast furnaces.
companies.opportunity: Find comparable unoptimized furnaces and verify metered savings.
constraints: The supplier-reported Seattle improvement already happened; it is not remaining gap there.
Applicability to other unoptimized equipment is unverified.
Electricity savings cannot be translated into climate damage without an appropriate electricity emissions factor.
The separate 7.23% hot-rolled intensity target gap is a target scenario, not a validated technology frontier.
steps: Separate Nucor’s existing electric-arc process from hypothetical blast-furnace conversions.
A Seattle case reports 5% furnace electricity savings from controls.
Use 50 MWh per 1,000 qualifying baseline MWh as a conditional replication benchmark.
Identify still-unoptimized assets before assigning an enterprise total.

companies.name: JPMorgan Chase
companies.boundary: Borrower-level physical interventions not yet identified
companies.summary: A bank’s biggest opportunity may sit in the assets it finances. A lower portfolio footprint is not proof that physical emissions fell.
companies.formula: Not quantified: named borrower assets, intervention baselines and causal financing evidence required.
companies.opportunity: Originate asset-specific loans with measurable physical improvements and contracted repayment.
constraints: Financed emissions overlap the emissions of borrowers. Do not add both to a portfolio harm total.
Selling a loan or changing attribution can lower reported financed emissions without physical reductions.
No defensible bank-wide preventable percentage has been established.
Modeled societal damage is not revenue available to return investment principal.
steps: Keep operational and financed emissions separate.
Identify a named borrower asset and its physical baseline.
Model the available alternative and determine whether funding causes extra or earlier adoption.
Quantify only after project evidence and repayable cashflows are established.
